newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk workers, employers in anti-Islamist protest.
newsitem.headline: Turk workers, employers in anti-Islamist protest.

text.p: Workers and employers at Turkish offices and factories stopped work briefly on Friday in a joint protest against an Islamist upsurge under the government of Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan.
Protesters read out a joint statement in workplaces at 1100 a.m (0800 GMT) accusing the coalition of spending more time on disputes over religion than on solving Turkey's acute economic problems.
"There are those who want to take our country back to the Middle Ages, to destroy democracy and human rights with fundamentalism," read the statement.

"The instability and tension has halted new investment and damaged existing investments," it said. The statement was signed by two trade union confederations of more than 500,000 workers, a trade group and two top business organisations.
Erbakan, modern Turkey's first Islamist leader, has been under fire from the army and other secularists for plans to introduce mild Islamist reforms.
His coalition says it is seeking early elections to clear up the uncertainty, which has hit government plans for a balanced budget and greater privatisation.
Analysts say the Turkish economy, already struggling under annual inflation of around 75 percent and gaping deficits, would suffer further if snap polls went ahead.
Around 300 workers and passers-by gathered at the Bahcelievler district council offices in Istanbul where Ridvan Budak, head of the DISK union confederation, read out the statement.
"Turkey is secular and will stay that way," workers shouted.

The once-mighty Turkish Left has been weakened by a 1980 military coup and subsequent free-marketeering civilian governments but workers' pay protests helped bring down a coalition government headed by Tansu Ciller in 1995.
